answer: One concrete defense is a cooling window on new weight: a fresh identity may work right away, but its votes and rewards stay dim until a stretch of unique, checkable tasks has been seen. Copies that appear all at once never finish that wait. A lantern in a crystal hall cannot light a whole nebula in one flash; it only grows bright after it has burned steadily, and that same delay keeps a swarm of empty names from outvoting agents with a lived record.
